label: PF Backlog 674
title: Review material-change decision API and correct delta-review base
body: Review budget blocks legitimate fix deltas because HIL MATERIAL_CHANGE decisions cannot be recorded through the backlog API, and re-review base selection rejects a valid earlier reviewed head. Add an operator-only decisions endpoint and make delta-budget exemption require a reviewed ancestor base plus a reason citing the latest review SHA.

brief.problem: HIL MATERIAL_CHANGE cannot be recorded via API; review budget blocks valid fix deltas.
brief.what_adds: Operator-only decisions endpoint plus reviewed-ancestor delta base.
brief.why: Keeps review enforcement compliant while allowing evidence-based re-reviews.

objective: Unblock legitimate fix deltas without weakening review-budget enforcement or requiring direct backlog mutation.
acceptance_criteria: The backlog API exposes an operator-only endpoint to append a MATERIAL_CHANGE decision with mode, reason, HIL confirmation and revision guard, and the item stores it for review_budget.
Delta re-review budget exemption accepts any reviewed ancestor as --since, requires the reason to cite the latest review SHA, and rejects arbitrary caller-supplied SHAs.
Tests cover API auth/validation, decision persistence, accepted reviewed-ancestor delta, and rejection of arbitrary or non-reviewed bases.
in_scope: Review material-change decision API and correct delta-review base
approach: Add an operator-only decisions endpoint that appends validated MATERIAL_CHANGE decisions through core.backlog.update, and fix architect_review delta budget to accept any reviewed ancestor base with a reason citing the latest review SHA.
risks: A permissive decisions endpoint could bypass review; restrict to MATERIAL_CHANGE, require hil_confirmed and hil:<actor>, keep revision guard.
Arbitrary --since could bypass budget; require the SHA to be a reviewed head and an ancestor of HEAD.
rollback: Remove the decisions route and restore strict latest-SHA delta exemption; no data migration.

Gate 1.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=2d9a0b7d3ba6
BLOCKER:
  - none
MAJOR:
  - hil:<actor> validation method is unspecified: design requires the field but does not say it is verified against an authenticated identity/allowlist, so any operator could self-assert HIL confirmation and satisfy the guard at the new endpoint.
  - AC-2 requires the delta reason to cite the latest review SHA, but FR-2/design_pack contracts only list "refuse unreviewed/non-ancestor" and omit the reason-citation rule, leaving the AC-2 half of validation unimplemented/tested by design.
  - New network endpoint contract (guardrail 8/9) states no tenant/subject scoping for /items/{id}/decisions; with only "operator role" authz, item-ID enumeration could cross scope — design must declare scoping or explicitly assert single-tenant.
  - Design pack does not answer the design-guardrail checklist (CL-008): availability/defence-in-depth, observability depth, and invariant ordering are absent; only rollback and tests are addressed.
MINOR:
  - Rollback claims "code revert only / no data migration", but append-only decisions written via the new route persist after revert with no purge/statement of post-rollback handling.
  - Observability is limited to "API errors and budget output": no structured log/metric for decision appends, HIL rejections, or budget refusals (guardrail 10).
  - Append ordering/sequence invariant is not stated (append-only yes, but ordering and duplicate-POST behavior beyond the revision guard is undefined).
  - Failure matrix defines only VALIDATION_FAILED while FR-1 declares 400/404/409; error-code contract is not aligned across design_pack and functional spec.
  - Language-rule classification of the new route (new shipped logic vs. edit to shipped Python in api/routers/backlog.py) should be explicitly asserted in the design.
NIT:
  - FR-3 test only asserts route existence in OpenAPI; a contract snapshot/diff would catch schema drift more reliably.
  - "no added runtime latency" NFR has no stated measurement or threshold.
SUMMARY:
  - Design is directionally sound (operator-only, append-only, revision guard, reviewed-ancestor + ancestor-of-HEAD check, tests with a named failing test), and rollback is code-only with no migration.
  - Top risks: unspecified HIL actor verification, missing reason-cites-latest-SHA rule in FR-2 contracts, and undefined tenant/subject scoping on the new endpoint — all must be resolved before Gate 1.5.
  - Guardrail checklist responses (availability, observability, invariants) and error-code contract alignment should be added to the design pack.
RECOMMENDATION: no hard blocker (MAJOR/MINOR/NIT advisory; HIL decides)
